issues.title: UNRESOLVED from the 10:24 playtest: "critical ladder bug, it's translated into the local thing"
issues.body:
From Pip's recorded playtest, 2026-07-31 **[12:45]**:

> *"critical ladder bug, it's translated into the local thing"*

## Status: not understood

Filed deliberately **without** a diagnosis. Two readings, and the grep-level extract cannot separate them:

1. **Local/global board confusion** -- the player cannot tell which board they are looking at. Adjacent to **[12:33]** *"it shows up showing as local, I still can't tell which one is mine"* (own-run highlighting, #957).
2. **An actual ladder-epoch fault** -- something keyed on `L3` leaking into or being overwritten by the local board file.

Reading 2 would be serious: the ladder epoch is the board key, and a silent fork of it is the failure the version-SSOT gate exists to prevent.

## Next step

**Needs Pip or the audio** -- 30 seconds of listening around 12:45 settles which reading is right. Not actionable before that, and guessing would be worse than waiting.

issues.title: Play Again / Back after a run ends: "there wasn't a game to play again from"
issues.body:
From Pip's recorded playtest, 2026-07-31 **[5:50]**:

> *"there wasn't a game to play again from, that logic seems weird"*

## What to check

The post-run navigation. After a run ends, Play Again / Back appears to offer a route that has nothing behind it, or refuses in a way that reads as broken rather than as a deliberate constraint.

Related and worth reading first: the scene-reentry run-killer family (#979, #983) and `pregame_setup.gd`'s header assumption that it is only ever reachable pre-run. `GameManager.start_new_game` refuses without `force=true` when a game is live, and `push_warning` on that path is invisible to a player -- a refusal that looks like a dead button.

**Now more likely to be hit**, because "Accept Your Fate" (#959 / PR #1051) shipped today and gives players a deliberate route to the end of a run. More players will reach this screen on purpose.

## Ask

Reproduce, then either make the route work or make the refusal legible. Not a silent no-op.

issues.title: Let the player set player name + lab name on the FIRST screen (not only in setup)
issues.body:
From Pip's recorded playtest, 2026-07-31 **[13:40]**:

> *"it's critical that we put the player name and lab name in there, it's critical that we let people update that on the first screen."*

And **[6:28]**: cannot click a name field to change it.

## Two halves, and only one is already tracked

- **Display** the name + lab on the board -- covered by #812 and #957.
- **Update them on the first screen** -- this issue. Not obviously covered anywhere.

## Why it matters tonight and after

Identity is what makes a leaderboard entry mean anything to the person who earned it. A player who reaches the board under a stale or default name has no reason to care about the board. The remote submission is gated on a non-empty player + lab name (`_has_submittable_identity`), so a player who never finds where to set them is a player whose score **silently does not upload**.

That is the failure family from #1027: nothing errors, the run just never appears.

## Ask

An editable name + lab field on the first screen the player sees, not only behind pre-game setup. Plus: check the [6:28] report that a name field is unclickable -- if a field is present but dead, that is a separate bug and the more urgent half.

Source: `art_generated/audiodump/2026-07-31_10-24-00.transcript.md`

issues.title: Leaderboard: the Duration column is meaningless when the score is turns survived
issues.body:
From Pip's recorded playtest, 2026-07-31 **[4:49]**:

> *"Duration doesn't make sense, because these are all 6 and 13 seconds, so the duration column doesn't work."*

## The problem

The board shows real elapsed wall-clock time. The score is **turns survived** (ADR-0002). A column reading "6s" / "13s" next to a turns-survived ranking invites the reader to compare two runs on a number that means nothing about how well either was played -- and a fast clicker looks better than a careful one.

Worse on a league board where the whole point is comparability.

## Options

1. **Drop the column.** Smallest, honest.
2. **Replace with something that ranks**: doom integral (already the ADR-0002 tiebreak and already submitted), or turns.
3. **Keep it but label it as trivia**, visually demoted so nobody reads it as a ranking signal.

Recommend 1 or 2 -- an unremovable number on a leaderboard is read as a score whatever the header says.

## Note

`duration` is computed and submitted in `game_over_screen._persist_and_submit_score`. Removing the **column** is a display change; removing the **field** touches the submission contract, which is frozen per website #191. Do the display half only until the freeze lifts.

Source: `art_generated/audiodump/2026-07-31_10-24-00.transcript.md`

issues.title: bug reports die on the player's disk: the website intake is built, the game never calls it
issues.body:
Found 2026-07-31 while mapping what would actually reach Pip on league night. Both halves of a working bug pipeline exist. They are not connected.

## The game end

`godot/scripts/ui/bug_report_panel.gd:186` shows the player, verbatim:

> "Thanks! Saved locally to: %s
>
> This build does not send reports automatically yet -- please email that file to team@pdoom1.com so it reaches us."

So a player who hits a crash writes a file to their own disk and is asked to compose an email with an attachment. **Most people will not.** The honesty of that message is good -- an earlier version implied an auto-filed GitHub issue, which was a lie, and someone fixed it. But honest silence is still silence.

## The website end -- which is already built

`pdoom1-website/.github/workflows/bug-report.yml`, "Bug Report Intake":

```yaml
on:
  repository_dispatch:
    types: [bug-report]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      title: ...
      description: ...
      type: [bug, feature, documentation, performance]
      email: ...
      source: (web/game)
```

It already accepts a `repository_dispatch` and files the issue. **It even has a `source` input with `game` as an option** -- so somebody designed this expecting the game to call it.

## Why it matters tonight specifically

The league opens to friends-of-friends. Every bug they hit becomes a file on a stranger's disk that nobody will ever read, and the absence of reports will look like the absence of bugs.

**Same survivorship problem Pip named this morning about the resign gap:**

> "I as dev don't see the player quitting, just the ones that finish the game."

The board shows people who finished. The issue tracker will show people who finished *and* chose to write an email. Neither shows the person who crashed on turn three and closed the window.

## Not tonight

This is a network call from the shipped client and it is nowhere near the freeze. Filing it so it exists, not proposing it for today.

## What it needs when it is built

- A dispatch token the client can hold. **This is the whole design problem** -- the score API is already unauthenticated (see the XSS in pdoom1-website#202, and #1012), and a bug-report endpoint that anyone can POST to is an issue-spam vector pointed at your own tracker.
- The player must consent per-report, visibly. The panel already carries a privacy note; sending is a different promise from saving.
- Offline and failure handling: the local file stays the fallback, and the message must not claim a send that did not happen. **The current text is honest and the replacement must be at least as honest** -- "this build does not send" is much better than a cheerful lie.

Related: #1012 (no verification field reaches a submitted score), pdoom1-website#202 (unauthenticated API), #1038 (trust and provenance), #1027 (silent wrongness).

issues.title: convention: printed docs carry a next-review date and its TRIGGER, not just a print date
issues.body:
Pip's design, 2026-07-31, on getting a printer working and immediately spotting the hazard it creates.

## The problem paper makes worse

Every failure this week was a document that had drifted from reality: a README advertising a download that never existed, a settings menu naming a dead key, three platform notes with the wrong keybind, a release feed announcing v0.9.0 for eight months.

**Paper is the ultimate stale copy.** It cannot be updated, only reprinted, and it will sit in a folder being confidently wrong for a year. If op manuals and ritual sheets are going into sleeves, this needs a convention before the folder fills up.

## The convention

Pip's format, and the good part is the **trigger**:

```
build notes.html - printed 27 july 2026 - next revision due: September 2026
  - Epoch 14 postmortem - see #1324
```

A bare date only creates anxiety -- you read it in October, see July, and cannot tell whether that matters. **A date plus a trigger lets a reader do the math and make a snap judgement**: has the Epoch 14 postmortem happened? No? Then this is probably still fine.

Five fields:

| Field | Why |
|---|---|
| doc path | so the reader can find the live version |
| revision date | when the CONTENT last changed (not when printed) |
| printed date | when THIS paper was made -- the two differ, and the gap is the risk |
| next review due + trigger | the event that will outmode it, not just a date |
| issue ref | where the review gets tracked |

Plus one line that settles arguments: **"source of truth: the file. If this printout disagrees with it, the file wins."**

## Two tiers, per Pip

- **Obvious rotators** (release notes, runsheets, league sheets) get a real trigger tied to an event -- an epoch cut, a postmortem, a version.
- **Everything else** gets a **yearly review** by default, "even if it's just me and an LLM going 'yup, this still works'". That is a low enough bar to actually happen, which is the whole point.

## First adopter

`docs/guides/RECORDING_SETUP_OBS.md` carries the footer as of today, with the trigger "first month of routine recorded sessions, or immediately on moving rooms / changing mic" -- a real event, not a guessed date.

## Where it should spread

- `docs/rituals/*` -- most likely to be printed, most costly to be stale. Their trigger is the Council of Elders amendment path (#1025).
- `tools/runsheet/*.html` -- dated by nature; should say so on the page.
- `tools/runsheet/playtest_card.html` -- already carries "Revised 2026-07-30"; wants the other four fields.
- Anything that ends up in the sleeve folder.

## Relationship to the wider pattern

This is #1027's thesis applied to paper: **make the implicit explicit and checkable.** A document that states its own expiry can be audited by a human at a glance, which is the cheapest possible instance of the semantic-invariant idea. Related: #1018 (ADR supersession -- the same problem, in git rather than in a folder).

issues.title: Ecosystem coherence: pdoom-data ADR-007 (anti-corruption layer) and ADR-008 (provenance/annotation model)
issues.body:
pdoom-data ratified two ADRs on 2026-07-31 that change how the ecosystem's repositories should talk to each other. **No action required in pdoom1 code today.** This is a request to scan and confirm coherence, at whatever pace suits, so philosophies do not quietly diverge.

Full text: `docs/adr/ADR-007-anti-corruption-layer.md` and `docs/adr/ADR-008-provenance-and-annotation-model.md` in pdoom-data.

---

## ADR-007: anti-corruption layer

**pdoom-data will never encode pdoom1's internal vocabulary.**

Trigger: our `event_v1` carries `impacts`, `rarity` and `pdoom_impact`, which are your mechanical vocabulary sitting in our shared schema. Your ADR-0015 deprecated exactly that shape on 2026-07-13. We treated that not as a one-off to patch but as evidence the structure was wrong.

Going forward, any directional hint we ship is expressed against an external, stable taxonomy -- currently the MIT AI Risk Repository domains -- plus a direction and confidence, attributed. **The mapping from our taxonomy onto your intermediaries lives in pdoom1.**

The reason is in your interest rather than ours: if we encoded `deployment_pressure` and you renamed it, every exported pack already in the wild would silently mean the wrong thing. No error, no failed parse, just numbers attached to a concept that no longer exists. With an external taxonomy you revise one mapping table and every historical pack stays correct -- so DQ-21 can change as often as the design needs.

We also adopted your framing verbatim rather than paraphrasing: **events are cards, the doom function is the rules.** Object if that misrepresents ADR-0015's intent.

### What we would like from pdoom1

- A scan for anywhere pdoom1 assumes pdoom-data will supply mechanical values (`impacts`, `rarity`, `pdoom_impact`). Those fields are now **archival** -- retained because the repo is an archive of its own evolution, but not current guidance and not to be authored against.
- DQ-21 status, which we also asked in #1052.

## ADR-008: provenance and annotation model

Relevant to pdoom1 because the contribution loop runs through the game.

**Three record types, joined by id, never one type with more fields:** fact (immutable), annotation (an attributed opinion about a fact), reception (what an audience did with a fact). The anti-pollution rule is a test rather than a discipline: *delete every annotation and reception record -- is the dataset still complete and correct?*

**We copy W3C vocabularies rather than inventing our own, and rather than fully adopting the standards.** PROV-O terms (`Entity`, `Activity`, `Agent`, `wasDerivedFrom`, `wasAttributedTo`) and Web Annotation terms (`target`, `body`, `creator`, `motivation`) used verbatim as field names, in plain JSON, no RDF. Pip's reasoning: troubleshooting then benefits from their known solution sets.

**If pdoom1 emits anything provenance-shaped, please use the same terms.** Two repos with `wasDerivedFrom` and `derived_from_ref` respectively is the avoidable version of this problem.

### Privacy decisions that bind the game side

Settled before anything is built, because retrofitting anonymity is the expensive direction:

- **In-game reactions carry no player identity at all.** Confirmed by Pip as consistent with pdoom1 being maximally privacy-respecting. Data minimisation by design, not by later stripping.
- **Reception data is per-person granularity but NOT per-identified-person** -- rows of respondents with stable pseudonymous ids. Pre-aggregation is refused because it destroys the analysis irreversibly.
- **Attribution is opt-in with a persisted contributor preference**, applied across channels rather than re-asked each time.
- **A preference change is prospective only.** Copies already taken cannot be recalled; that is a property of publishing. This must be stated to contributors at opt-in.
- **The bar is institutional usability, not minimum compliance.** A collaborator's institution should be able to approve use of this data.

**Channels are never summed.** Forty deliberated website comments must not vanish into ten thousand reflexive in-game clicks. Distinct annotation sets, distinct motivations, consumer weights them.

### What we would like from pdoom1

- Confirm the no-player-identity property holds for any reaction telemetry you would send upstream.
- Flag early if any planned in-game feedback mechanism would need identity, because that is a decision to make deliberately rather than discover.

## Nothing is built yet

Both ADRs are blocked on pdoom-data#43 and your DQ-21. Filed now so the shape is agreed while it is fresh, not after schemas exist.

Related: pdoom1#1052, pdoom1 ADR-0015, pdoom-data #27 #34 #39 #43 #47 #48 #49

issues.title: build_release: refuse to build from a stale or dirty tree -- prove build-matches-INTENT, not just pack-matches-build
issues.body:
Noted by Pip 2026-07-31 for the Saturday mortem, from a hand-run habit that had to be repeated three times in two days.

## The habit worth automating

Before every cut this week, the ritual was a hand-written grep block:

```
grep -c "weekly-2026-w31" godot/autoload/game_config.gd
grep -c "LadderExplainer" godot/scenes/leaderboard_screen.tscn
grep -c "Reserve Attention" godot/scenes/main.tscn
grep -c "Accept Your Fate" godot/scenes/pause_menu.tscn
```

**Do not save that.** A hand-maintained list of strings-to-check is the exact anti-pattern this repo keeps hitting (see the stale `decisions/README.md`, the hand-maintained release feed #1008, the drifted keybind labels #1011). It only ever knows what someone remembered to add, and it is stale the moment the next fix lands.

## The invariant underneath it

**Do not build from a tree that is not what the builder thinks it is.**

That is generic, needs no maintenance, and would have caught every instance.

## The precise gap in what we already have

`tools/build_release.py` is genuinely good at one half of this. It nukes `godot/.godot`, forces a reimport, exports, and **proves a unique freshness marker is inside the emitted `.pck`** before it will hand over an artifact.

That proves **the pack matches the build run.**

It does not prove **the build run matches the intent.** Nothing checks that the working tree corresponds to the commit the human believes they are shipping. Both near-misses this week lived in exactly that gap:

1. **2026-07-30 ~08:50** -- Pip was about to cut with a checkout **7 commits behind** `origin/main` and `version.txt` still reading `0.13.1`. Caught by luck, not by a check. That build would have shipped the previous day's code under the wrong version, with none of the freeze in it.
2. **2026-07-31 ~08:55** -- the fast gate reported **990 tests / 95 files** instead of 995 / 96. Nothing went red; the gate passed because the floor is 300. The cause was a stale local `main` missing a merged test file. Caught only because a *number moved*, and only because someone was watching the number rather than the status.

Note the shape of (2): **a green gate, running fewer tests than it should.** That is #640 recurring in a new place, and it is the reason a floor-based min-test check is not sufficient on its own.

## Proposed check (argue with the shape, not just the details)

In `build_release.py`, before anything else, and loudly:

- [ ] `git fetch` the tracking remote, then **refuse to build if HEAD is behind it.** This alone catches both incidents.
- [ ] **Refuse, or require an explicit `--allow-dirty`, if the working tree has uncommitted changes** to `godot/`. A release built from uncommitted state cannot be reproduced by anyone, including its author.
- [ ] **Print the exact commit, branch, and behind/ahead counts** at the top of the run, so the human sees what they are actually shipping before the long part starts.
- [ ] Consider asserting the **test-file count did not decrease** versus the previous run, rather than only checking a floor. A dropping count is the tell that a floor cannot see.

Escape hatches must exist (building from a branch mid-review is legitimate) but should be **explicit flags, not defaults** -- the failure mode is someone not realising, so a silent default defeats it.

## Why this belongs to #1027 rather than being a one-off

This is a **semantic invariant**, not a syntax gate: the file parsed, the build ran, the pack was provably fresh, and the artifact was still wrong. The guardrails catch bad code and miss wrong state. This is one of the concrete instances #1027 asks for -- and it names a real failure it would have caught, which is the bar that issue sets for accepting a new check.

It also pairs with **#1038** (build provenance and attestation): "prove the artifact came from a known commit" is the same claim, one aimed inward at the builder and one aimed outward at a stranger.

## For the Saturday mortem

Related: #1026 (five whys), #1027 (phase transition / semantic invariants), #1038 (trust and provenance), #640 (the original hollow gate), #1036 (tests passing by ordering accident).

issues.title: ADR-0015 / DQ-21: what should a pdoom-data event carry, now that literal doom fields are deprecated?
issues.body:
From pdoom-data. Two questions, one blocking and one design-level. Read-only investigation on our side; no changes made to pdoom1.

## Context

pdoom-data ships `event_v1` records carrying `impacts: [{variable, change}]`, `rarity` and `pdoom_impact`. **ADR-0015 (accepted 2026-07-13) deprecates exactly that shape:**

> No action or event definition carries a literal doom field. Effects target intermediary world-state variables ... doom is computed from world state each day tick.

So our schema is currently handing you the "single source-destination number bumps" that ADR names as legacy. We want to stop doing that. We do **not** want to guess our way to a replacement, because ADR-0015 point 2 says adding an intermediary is an ADR-grade act — and inventing your mechanical vocabulary from outside your repo would be exactly the wrong move.

We also found two candidate vocabularies and could not tell which is live:

| Source | Vocabulary |
|---|---|
| ADR-0015 examples, marked "v1 vocabulary owed, DQ-21" | lab capability, deployment pressure, governance quality, public salience |
| `godot/docs/design/RISK_SYSTEM.md` (2025-12-25, "In Development") | Capability Overhang, Research Integrity, Regulatory Attention, Public Awareness, Insider Threat, Financial Exposure |

## Question 1 (blocking us)

**What is DQ-21's status and rough timeline?** We have a consumer-facing export profile blocked on it (pdoom-data#43). Blocked is the correct state — we are not looking to route around it — but knowing whether it is weeks or months changes what we build meanwhile.

Also: is `RISK_SYSTEM.md` superseded by ADR-0015, or are the six risk pools the intended v1 intermediaries under a different name?

## Question 2 (the design one)

**What do you actually want an event to carry?**

Our current thinking is that the answer might be "nothing mechanical at all" — that events cross the boundary as facts plus clearly-attributed editorial opinion, and every mechanical consequence is computed inside pdoom1. That would be the cleanest version of the firewall either repo has managed, and it would make our export profile simpler rather than harder.

If you do want a directional hint, our proposal is that it should be expressed **in a vocabulary pdoom-data owns and can defend** — for example the MIT AI Risk Repository domains we already tag against, plus a direction and a confidence — rather than in your internal variable names. You would keep a mapping table from our stable taxonomy onto your intermediaries.

The reason is deliberately in your interest: it means DQ-21 can change, and change again, **without churning our data**. Only your mapping table moves. Standard anti-corruption layer between two bounded contexts. If instead we encoded your intermediaries directly, every vocabulary revision would require a schema version bump and a re-export on our side, and stale copies in the wild would silently mean the wrong thing.

## A framing we would like to adopt from you

ADR-0015 point 4 states our boundary better than our own docs do:

> The doom function is structure; intermediary pricing is numbers ... MtG framing: events are cards, the doom function is the rules.

We propose adopting that verbatim in pdoom-data's glossary rather than maintaining a parallel vocabulary. pdoom-data ships cards; pdoom1 owns the rules. Object if that misrepresents the intent.

## Related

- pdoom-data#43 — export profile, blocked on this
- pdoom-data#34 — moving pdoom1's resource model out of our shared schema
- pdoom-data#27 — Hop A ratification, where the monthly World-Update Pack was agreed
- pdoom1#962 — frontier-labs integration (unblocked, dataset shipped)

issues.title: ADR set: correctness/staleness/cohesion pass, and an implementation-status field the website can render
issues.body:
Raised by Pip 2026-07-31, from the website side, after a honesty sweep found that the
website's published rendering of these ADRs makes claims the ADRs themselves do not
support.

## Why this is urgent-ish rather than tidy-up

`pdoom1-website` renders 17 of these ADRs to **public pages** at
`https://pdoom1.com/design-notes/`, via `scripts/sync/sync-design-notes.py`. The
generator wraps every page in framing text that reads:

> These are the actual decision records the game is built from … They describe *why*
> the game works the way it does.

That framing is **present tense and uniform**, and it is false for at least three:

- **ADR-0005** (emergent waves / seed schedules) is published as live design, but
  pdoom1#1020 states: *"ADR-0005 seed schedules are INERT in real play: nothing passes a
  schedule to GameState, so `event_schedule` is always empty."* The page even tells a
  player that *"the turn-9 funding wave on this week's seed becomes community
  vocabulary"* — a mechanic that does not fire. A league player could plan around it.
- **ADR-0003** (Liability Ledger) appears in the roadmap under *"Further out — wanted,
  not scheduled"*.
- **ADR-0007**'s own status says *build **third**, strictly after ADR-0003 and ADR-0004* —
  i.e. not built.

The website will fix its own framing. But the underlying question is yours: **which of
these records describe shipped behaviour, and which describe intent?** Nothing in the
current format distinguishes them, so no downstream consumer can either.

## What Pip is asking for

1. **A correctness / staleness / cohesion pass over the whole ADR set.** For each:
   is it accurate today, superseded, partially implemented, or aspirational?
2. **A machine-readable implementation status.** The website already renders the
   `Status:` line verbatim, so an added field — e.g. `Implemented: yes | partial | no` —
   would let the published page say `ACCEPTED — not yet implemented` automatically,
   with no website change beyond reading one field. This is the smallest fix that
   removes the whole class.
3. **Vocabulary drift.** ADR-0011 describes *"Current build: one global AP pool"* — the
   AP pool has since been removed for the attention economy (pdoom1#1037 is already
   sweeping stale AP wording). "Current build" is unambiguously present tense on a page
   dated three weeks ago. Consider a convention: never write *"current build"* in a
   record that outlives the build.
4. **Publication pipeline.** `sync-design-notes.yml` renders from the latest **release
   tag**, so ADR-0018 (on `main` since 2026-07-27) is not published and a reader cannot
   tell. That is defensible, but it is undocumented. Decide and document: do design
   notes track `main` or the last release? Then make the rendered page state which.

## Cross-repo note

`docs/PLAN_EVENT_INTEGRATION.md` still describes `historical_events.json` as
*"20 events, OLD format"* — it now holds 1,194. And `CHANGELOG.md` has no mention of
`pdoom-data`, `historical_events` or `EventService` at all, so the integration that
~2,190 published website pages describe is undocumented in the game's own changelog.
Worth folding into the same pass.

Filed from pdoom1-website so it is not lost. Happy to take any part of this on the
website side.

issues.title: design(tempo): actions resolve instantly, so the early game has no rhythm -- time, sequencing, and the queue's promise
issues.body:
From Pip's recorded playtest of the re-cut 0.13.2 artifact, 2026-07-30 16:36. Transcript in `art_generated/audiodump/2026-07-30_16-36-55.transcript.md`.

Three observations that look separate and are one problem.

## 1. Nothing takes time

**[1:33]** *"we don't have any of the other actions taking time yet, I think, which is kind of throwing off some of the sequences. So like all the fundraising -- if I go and look at the plan, all of the fundraising happens on July the 4th, whereas what we need to do is have them take some time and then return a result later."*

Twenty actions were queued in about fifteen seconds and every one resolved on the same in-game date. There is no lead time, no in-flight period, and therefore no reason to sequence anything.

**This is upstream of a bug already fixed.** The action queue overflowed off-screen (#1039) partly *because* nothing leaves the queue -- instant resolution means the queue is a list of everything you have ever clicked this turn rather than a set of things currently happening. Widening the container treats the symptom.

It also undercuts the game's own deepest stated rule -- *"tragedy requires lead time"* -- which cannot be felt by the player if nothing the player does has any.

## 2. The early game does not teach the loop

**[4:33]** *"a little bit of a workshopping on making what actions players can and should be taking easier and more obvious by unlocking them more sequentially during the early game. We can give people options... but we encourage people to take maybe one of each of the higher network, fundraise, and other sets of actions so that people get used to sending things off, and we need to combine that with the things taking time so people are used to having stuff coming back."*

The ask is a **send-and-return rhythm**: dispatch something, wait, get a result. That rhythm cannot be taught while everything resolves instantly, which is why this and (1) are the same issue.

## 3. The queue should promise a completion time

**[5:02]** *"we probably want something like the action queuing system to have implied when are these things going to be done by us, but we need to think about that carefully."*

Once actions take time, the queue stops being a list and becomes a **schedule**. It should say when each thing lands. Pip flags this as wanting care, and it does -- it is the difference between a queue and a calendar, and it changes what the Plan screen is for.

## Why one issue

(2) is unteachable without (1). (3) is meaningless without (1) and is the natural UI consequence of it. Designing them separately produces a timing system with no onboarding and a queue that does not reflect it.

## Constraints already known

- **This forks the ladder.** Action durations change what happens on a fixed seed, so any implementation is an epoch bump (`RELEASE_NOMENCLATURE.md`). Not a patch.
- **Not this league.** Pip: *"it's a UI thing, so it doesn't need to change the ladder"* -- that was about the layout half (#1043). The timing half absolutely does change the ladder, and the distinction is worth keeping crisp.
- ADR-0011 effort economy and the founder-hours split are the substrate this lands on; ADR-0009's no-banking rule constrains what "in flight across a month boundary" can mean.

## Related

- #1043 -- the Plan-screen layout brief from the same afternoon; the dead middle is a candidate home for a schedule view
- #1041 -- morning playtest findings, incl. hiring actions not creating queue cards, which is the same queue-is-not-a-schedule confusion
- #1039 -- the overflow fix that treated the symptom
- #822 -- overbook TEETH, adjacent forcing-function work

issues.title: feat(engine): integrate frontier-labs dataset (pdoom-data#37); expose a list the website can pull to fix calculate-game-stats
issues.body:
## Ask (follow-on from pdoom-data#37)

Once pdoom-data ships its first-pass frontier-labs dataset (**PipFoweraker/pdoom-data#37** — foundation dates 2000→present), build the follow-on:

1. **Integrate** the frontier-labs list + foundation dates into the game engine (labs as timeline entities that come into existence on their founding dates).
2. **As soon as the MVP is enough for the website to consume it**, expose it so pdoom1-website can pull the list — so we can retire the hardcoded lab list in `calculate-game-stats.py` and drive `frontier_labs_count` (and future stats) from real data.

## Why

pdoom1-website currently hardcodes the frontier-labs list in `scripts/calculate-game-stats.py` to produce a stubbed count. Per the cross-repo protocol (game/data own truth; the website derives), that count should come from the canonical dataset. This also feeds the website's planned "state of doom" stats page.

## Sequencing (please don't block the website on full engine work)

`pdoom-data#37` → **engine integration** → **expose a consumable artifact**. The website does **not** need the full engine integration — it just needs a **stable, fetchable list** of `{id, name, founded, status}`. Please ship that consumable early (a served JSON, or simply point us at the pdoom-data serveable if that's cleaner) even if the richer engine timeline mechanics land later.

## Definition of done (for the website's needs)

- A documented, fetchable artifact of frontier labs + foundation dates.
- The URL + shape noted in a comment here so the pdoom1-website session can wire `calculate-game-stats.py` to it.

---
_Depends on pdoom-data#37. Filed as cross-repo work at Pip's direction (contact-protocol override, 2026-07-27) by the pdoom1-website session._

issues.title: Main-screen warnings: tell players the ladder can fork BEFORE they play (draft copy inside)
issues.body:
Requested by Pip, 2026-07-30: *"Maybe we can have a more explicit set of warnings posted
on the main page of the UI of the game."* Context is the L2 -> L3 mid-month fork and his
own note that **"ladder integrity will probably break this week, that's fine and
expected"** — the point being that players should learn that from the game, not from
finding their score gone.

Drafted from the website side because the same statement has to appear on
`/leaderboard/`, and the two should not say different things. **The game's wording is
the authority; the website will follow whatever lands here.** Reword freely.

## The principle worth keeping, whatever the wording

A player who loses a score should have been told it could happen **before** they played,
not consoled afterwards. The warning is cheap; the trust is not. Three things follow:

1. **State the risk, not a reassurance.** "May be reset" is honest. "Your scores are
   safe" is a promise the alpha cannot keep.
2. **Never claim a score is permanent.** Scores are keyed to a ladder epoch and epochs
   fork. That is by design, and it should read as design, not as an accident.
3. **Say it where the decision is made** — before the run, on the screen a player looks
   at when choosing to play, not buried in a settings page or a changelog.

## Suggested copy

### A. Persistent line on the main/welcome screen

Short enough to live permanently without becoming wallpaper:

> **ALPHA — scores and rules change between releases.**
> Leaderboards are tied to a rules version. When the rules change, a new board opens and
> earlier scores stay on the old one.

### B. Expanded panel (behind an "i" / "What does that mean?" affordance)

> **P(Doom)1 is in alpha, and the rules are still moving.**
>
> Each leaderboard is tied to a **ladder epoch** — a snapshot of the game's rules. When a
> release changes how the game plays, a new epoch opens and a fresh board starts.
>
> **Your earlier scores are not deleted, and they are not carried forward either.** They
> stay on the board for the rules they were set under. A score from before a rules change
> cannot be fairly compared to one set after it, so we do not merge them.
>
> This will happen again. It is how the game stays honest about what a score means,
> rather than maintaining one ever-growing table that quietly mixes incompatible runs.
>
> Right now: **epoch L3**, opened 2026-07-31.

### C. One-time notice when the epoch changes under a returning player

Fires when the local build's ladder epoch differs from the one last seen:

> **New rules, new board.**
> The rules changed since you last played, so a new leaderboard has opened. Your previous
> scores are still recorded under the old rules — they are just not on this board.

## Two specifics that make this concrete this week

- The L3 fork removed the action-point pool entirely in favour of an attention economy,
  added office lease + lock-in, four-way founder hours, six previously-inert upgrades and
  a quirk rebalance. That is a big enough change that a player who does not know the
  board reset will assume a bug.
- **A small number of testers have genuinely stranded scores from before the fork.** Pip
  is contacting them personally, which is the right call — but the warning above is what
  stops the same conversation being needed next epoch.

## Where the epoch string should come from

`GameConfig.get_board_version()` / `ladder_version.txt`, rendered — **not typed into the
scene**. A hardcoded "L3" in a `.tscn` becomes a lie at the next fork, and this is a
warning whose whole job is to be true. Same class as pdoom1#1011 (derive keybind labels
rather than typing them) and the F8/N bug that came from typing a key into three files.

## Website side

Whatever lands here, `/leaderboard/` will carry a matching statement so a player who
never opens the game's welcome screen still sees it. Tracked at pdoom1-website#201.
Please comment here with the final wording, or just ship it and I will follow the scene
text.
